title: Charge of the records
summary: Nephi, son of Helaman, gives his eldest son Nephi charge concerning the plates of brass, the records, and sacred things. The elder Nephi departs from the land, and his son keeps the records in his stead.
characters: Nephi (eldest son of Nephi, son of Helaman)

explicit_facts.text: The ninety-first year had passed; it was six hundred years since Lehi left Jerusalem, and Lachoneus was chief judge and governor over the land.
Nephi, son of Helaman, gave his eldest son Nephi charge concerning the plates of brass, the records, and things kept sacred.
The elder Nephi departed from the land; no one knew where he went. His son Nephi kept the records in his stead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two Nephis may be shown together for the giving of the charge.
The records may be visible without implying a physical handoff.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise place where the charge was given.
The appearance of the people, records, and surroundings.

narration.text: giving charge unto his son Nephi, who was his eldest son
his son Nephi did keep the records in his stead

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Lehi's departure from Jerusalem is a chronological reference, not an event occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an arrival or destination for the elder Nephi.
Do not invent spoken words or show a physical handoff as an explicit event.
Do not depict Lehi or Lachoneus as present.

title: Doubt and rejoicing
summary: At the beginning of the ninety-second year, signs and miracles increase. Some say the time for Samuel's words to be fulfilled has passed and taunt believers.

explicit_facts.text: At the beginning of the ninety-second year, there were greater signs and miracles among the people.
Some said the time had passed for Samuel the Lamanite's prophecies to be fulfilled.
Some rejoiced over believers and said their joy and faith had been vain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The unbelievers address or mock believers.
unspecified_visual_details: What the signs and miracles look like; the setting and appearance of the people.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold the time is past, and the words of Samuel are not fulfilled;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: those who disbelieve

spoken_dialogue.text: therefore, your joy and your faith concerning this thing hath been vain.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: those who disbelieve

narration.text: there began to be greater signs and greater miracles

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a particular miracle or sign not described in the verses.

title: Believers watch
summary: A great uproar spreads through the land. Believers grieve but watch steadfastly for the promised day and night that would be as one day without night.

explicit_facts.text: A great uproar occurred throughout the land, and believers were sorrowful that the prophecies might not come to pass.
Believers watched steadfastly for the day and night and day that would be as one day, without night.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Believers watch through the anticipated time, appearing sorrowful and attentive.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and time of day; how the watching is arranged.

narration.text: they did watch steadfastly for that day and that night and that day

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the promised sign yet in this scene.

title: A day set apart
summary: Unbelievers set a day to kill those who believe unless Samuel's sign comes. Nephi, son of Nephi, sees the wickedness and is exceedingly sorrowful.

explicit_facts.text: Unbelievers set apart a day to put believers to death unless Samuel's sign came.
Nephi, son of Nephi, saw the wickedness of his people and was exceedingly sorrowful.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi reacts with visible sorrow to the threat against believers.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, how the day is announced, and whether the threatened believers are present with Nephi.

narration.text: his heart was exceedingly sorrowful

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an execution or an attack; none is narrated here.

title: Nephi's prayer
summary: Nephi goes out, bows to the earth, and cries mightily to God for the believers facing destruction. He cries all day; the Lord's voice comes to him.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi went out and bowed himself to the earth, praying for believers about to be destroyed for their faith.
He cried mightily to the Lord all day, and the Lord's voice came to him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is shown bowed on the ground in prayer.
unspecified_visual_details: The place where Nephi prays; the Lord's visible appearance, if any.

narration.text: he went out and bowed himself down upon the earth
the voice of the Lord came unto him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is described as a voice; no visible appearance is stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly or invent a form for the voice.

title: The Lord's promise
summary: The Lord tells Nephi to be of good cheer: the sign will come that night, and the Lord will come into the world on the morrow. He says he comes to fulfill what was spoken and to do the will of the Father and the Son.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says the sign will be given that night and he will come into the world on the morrow.
The Lord says he comes to fulfill all things made known and to do the will of the Father and the Son.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi listens while the Lord speaks off-screen.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible appearance of the Lord; Nephi's precise location and posture during the speech.

spoken_dialogue.text: Lift up your head and be of good cheer;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: for behold, the time is at hand, and on this night shall the sign be given,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and on the morrow come I into the world,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I come unto my own,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Keep the Lord's voice off-screen; the text supplies no visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord's birth or give the Lord a visible form.

title: No darkness at sunset
summary: At sunset there is no darkness. The people are astonished; many unbelievers fall to the earth as if dead when they realize their plan to destroy believers has been frustrated.

explicit_facts.text: At sunset there was no darkness, and the people were astonished.
Many who had not believed fell to the earth as if dead, knowing their plan of destruction had been frustrated.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sky or surroundings remain light after sunset; some people lie fallen.
unspecified_visual_details: The source and quality of the light; the specific place and number of people.

narration.text: at the going down of the sun there was no darkness
fell to the earth and became as if they were dead

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict injury, death, or gore; the text says they fell as if dead.

title: The people fall
summary: People across the earth, north and south and from west to east, are astonished and fall to the earth. They recognize the prophets' testimony and fear because of their iniquity and unbelief.

explicit_facts.text: People throughout the earth, from west to east and in the north and south lands, were astonished and fell to the earth.
They knew the prophets had testified for many years and feared because of their iniquity and unbelief.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A montage may show people falling in distinct places, without combining them into one location.
unspecified_visual_details: The individual locations, identities, and appearances of these people.

narration.text: they fell to the earth
they began to fear because of their iniquity and their unbelief

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify or name any individual among the people.

title: Daylight through the night
summary: The night remains as light as midday. The sun rises in the morning according to its proper order, and the people know it is the day the Lord should be born. All things have occurred according to the prophets' words.

explicit_facts.text: There was no darkness all night; it was as light as midday.
The sun rose in the morning according to its proper order, and the people knew it was the day the Lord should be born.
All things occurred according to the words of the prophets.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show the uninterrupted light through night and the subsequent sunrise as distinct visual beats.
unspecified_visual_details: The source of nighttime light and the specific landscape.

narration.text: there was no darkness in all that night
all things, every whit, according to the words of the prophets

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord's birth, which is not narrated in these verses.

title: A new star
summary: A new star appears, according to the word.

explicit_facts.text: A new star appeared according to the word.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show a new star in the sky.

narration.text: a new star did appear

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the star as a particular astronomical object.

title: Belief amid deception
summary: Lies are sent among the people to harden hearts against the signs and wonders, but most believe and are converted. Nephi and many others baptize unto repentance, and the people begin again to have peace.

explicit_facts.text: Lies were sent among the people to harden hearts against belief in the signs and wonders; most believed and were converted to the Lord.
Nephi and many others baptized unto repentance; there was a great remission of sins, and the people began again to have peace.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and others perform baptisms; avoid showing the spiritual remission as a visible phenomenon.
unspecified_visual_details: How the lies are transmitted; the baptism setting and method.

narration.text: the more part of the people did believe
Nephi went forth among the people
baptizing unto repentance

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Satan is named as the source of lies, but no visible appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Satan or personify the lies as a visible figure.

title: A few begin to preach
summary: A few begin to preach, endeavoring to prove by the scriptures that observing the law of Moses is no longer expedient.
characters: A few unnamed people who begin to preach

explicit_facts.text: A few began to preach, endeavoring to prove by the scriptures that it was no more expedient to observe the law of Moses.
They erred because they had not understood the scriptures.
They soon became converted and were convinced of their error; in the same year, they confessed their faults.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show the initial preaching as one moment; do not depict the later conversion or confession as simultaneous.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and the preachers’ appearances.
The exact number of preachers and any listeners.

narration.text: And there were no contentions, save it were a few that began to preach, endeavoring to prove by the scriptures that it was no more expedient to observe the law of Moses.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse identifies the preachers’ claim as an error; verse 25 says the law was not yet fulfilled.
Their conversion and confession occur later and are not pictured in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the preachers’ spoken words or identify them.
Do not depict a visible revelation or combine the preaching with their later conversion and confession.

title: The ninety-second and ninety-third years
summary: The ninety-second year passed, bringing glad tidings because of signs that came to pass. The ninety-third year passed in peace except for Gadianton robbers who dwelt in the mountains, could not be overpowered by the people, and committed murders and slaughter.

explicit_facts.text: The ninety-second year passed, bringing glad tidings to the people because signs came to pass according to the prophets' prophecy.
The ninety-third year passed in peace except for Gadianton robbers who dwelt in the mountains, infested the land, and had holds and secret places so strong that the people could not overpower them.
The robbers committed many murders and much slaughter among the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The robbers' dwelling area is mountainous.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the signs, people, robbers, and mountain holds; the precise locations and timing of individual attacks.

narration.text: And thus the ninety and second year did pass away, bringing glad tidings unto the people
And it came to pass that the ninety and third year did also pass away in peace,
save it were for the Gadianton robbers, who dwelt upon the mountains,
therefore they did commit many murders, and did do much slaughter among the people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Keep the two years distinct; the verses summarize events rather than narrate one continuous moment.
Verses 24–25 were not supplied. Mark the transition to verse 26 without inventing or depicting intervening events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not specify what the signs looked like or invent the contents of verses 24–25.
Do not turn the summarized violence into a specific attack or show gore.

title: The robbers increase
summary: In the ninety-fourth year the Gadianton robbers increase greatly as many Nephite dissenters flee to them, causing sorrow among the Nephites who remain.
characters: Nephites who remained in the land

explicit_facts.text: In the ninety-fourth year the Gadianton robbers greatly increased because many Nephite dissenters fled to them, causing sorrow to the Nephites remaining in the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show dissenters joining the robbers and remaining Nephites grieving as separate visual moments.
unspecified_visual_details: The place where dissenters join the robbers and their appearance.

narration.text: there were many dissenters of the Nephites who did flee unto them

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent motives for the dissenters beyond the reported flight to the robbers.

title: The rising generation is led away
summary: Many Lamanite children grow up and become strong in years. Some Zoramites lead them away with lies and flattering words to join the Gadianton robbers. The Lamanites are afflicted, decreasing in faith and righteousness because of the rising generation's wickedness.
characters: Lamanite children who joined the robbers

explicit_facts.text: Many Lamanite children grew up and became strong in years; some Zoramites led them away with lies and flattering words to join the Gadianton robbers.
The Lamanites were afflicted and began to decrease in faith and righteousness because of the rising generation's wickedness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show the Zoramites leading the youths toward the robbers, with the resulting affliction as a distinct later moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The children’s ages and appearances, the route, and where the robbers are met.

narration.text: to join those Gadianton robbers
began to decrease as to their faith and righteousness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 30 summarizes consequences; it is not a separate narrated physical event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent specific lies, flattering speech, or individual motives.
